findings.title: Forward Secrecy Supported
findings.plain_explanation: The TLS 1.3 ServerHello key_share indicates ephemeral key exchange; the cipher name alone does not establish this.
findings.why_it_matters: Ephemeral key exchange ensures that recorded encrypted traffic cannot be decrypted retroactively even if server private keys are compromised at a later date.
findings.evidence: TLS 1.3 ServerHello key_share observed: 29.

evidence_items.description: TLS 1.3 ServerHello key_share observed: 29.

steps: No change is required by this observed check. Maintain the baseline and re-check a fresh capture after configuration changes.

findings.recommendation: Continue enforcing ephemeral key exchanges (ECDHE) across all mail transport connections.

findings.title: Cleartext Email Transport
findings.plain_explanation: This email session continued without TLS protection, allowing application-layer traffic to traverse the observed network path without transport encryption.
findings.why_it_matters: Cleartext email transport exposes message metadata, routing headers, and session contents to passive eavesdropping and traffic manipulation along the transit path.
findings.evidence: Identified SMTP session on port 587.; No TLS encryption handshake was negotiated for this session.; Session operated in CLEARTEXT (STARTTLS Offered but Not Used) mode.

evidence_items.description: Identified SMTP session on port 587.
No TLS encryption handshake was negotiated for this session.
Session operated in CLEARTEXT (STARTTLS Offered but Not Used) mode.

steps: Identify whether the endpoint is client submission, mailbox access, or Internet SMTP relay.
Require TLS on authenticated submission and mailbox access; test all clients before rollout. Do not blindly require TLS on public port 25, which can reject legitimate mail.
Capture a fresh session and verify the upgrade before authentication.

snippet.scope: Example parameter values for authenticated submission only. Translate to per-service master.cf overrides where appropriate. Requires a working TLS certificate/key. Do not apply globally to a public port-25 relay.

findings.recommendation: Enforce TLS encryption for all email communications using Direct TLS (e.g. port 465/993/995) or mandatory STARTTLS with strict rejection of unencrypted fallbacks.

findings.title: STARTTLS Available But Not Used
findings.plain_explanation: The server advertised STARTTLS, but the client continued the SMTP session without upgrading to TLS.
findings.why_it_matters: Transport encryption was available from the server, but the client did not initiate an upgrade. Without mandatory TLS enforcement, the session continued unprotected over cleartext.
findings.evidence: Server advertised STARTTLS capability.; No STARTTLS command or TLS handshake was observed.

evidence_items.description: Server advertised STARTTLS capability.
No STARTTLS command or TLS handshake was observed.

steps: Configure the affected client to require STARTTLS or the correct implicit-TLS port.
For authenticated submission, reject plaintext fallback after testing clients. Treat public relay policy separately.
Capture again and check the server selection and authentication order.

snippet.scope: Example parameter values for authenticated submission only. Translate to per-service master.cf overrides where appropriate. Requires a working TLS certificate/key. Do not apply globally to a public port-25 relay.

findings.recommendation: Configure the client and server policy to require TLS for this mail flow and reject insecure fallback where operationally appropriate.

findings.title: Authentication Before TLS
findings.plain_explanation: Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.
findings.why_it_matters: Transmitting authentication credentials over an unencrypted cleartext session exposes account login data to passive network capture and credential theft.
findings.evidence: SMTP authentication command (e.g. AUTH/LOGIN/USER) was observed on the wire.; Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.

evidence_items.description: SMTP authentication command (e.g. AUTH/LOGIN/USER) was observed on the wire.
Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.

steps: Require TLS before advertising or accepting authentication on the submission service.
Update affected clients and rotate potentially exposed credentials through your approved process.
Confirm in a fresh capture that authentication cannot occur in plaintext.

snippet.scope: Example parameter values for authenticated submission only. Translate to per-service master.cf overrides where appropriate. Requires a working TLS certificate/key. Do not apply globally to a public port-25 relay.

findings.recommendation: Configure the mail server to mandate STARTTLS before advertising or accepting AUTH commands.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS Version (TLS 1.0)
findings.plain_explanation: Observed email session negotiated deprecated TLS 1.0 protocol, which is susceptible to known downgrade attacks and lacks modern authenticated encryption.
findings.why_it_matters: TLS 1.0 is formally deprecated under RFC 8996 due to lack of modern cipher constructions, vulnerability to downgrade attacks, and security weaknesses.
findings.evidence: Server selected deprecated protocol version TLS 1.0.

evidence_items.description: Server selected deprecated protocol version TLS 1.0.

steps: Inventory ClientHello offers and upgrade clients that cannot offer TLS 1.2 or newer.
Set a TLS 1.2 minimum on the affected service after staging tests and a rollback plan.
Check both mandatory and opportunistic TLS settings for the intended service.

snippet.scope: Example parameter values for authenticated submission only. Translate to per-service master.cf overrides where appropriate. Requires a working TLS certificate/key. Do not apply globally to a public port-25 relay.

findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 on 198.51.100.25 and configure the mail server to require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 as the minimum acceptable protocol version.

findings.title: Weak / Deprecated Cipher Suite (TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA)
findings.plain_explanation: The session negotiated weak or deprecated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA, which is vulnerable to cryptanalytic attacks.
findings.why_it_matters: The selected cipher suite (TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA) utilizes obsolete algorithms (such as 64-bit block ciphers like 3DES vulnerable to Sweet32, or stream ciphers like RC4) susceptible to practical collision or plaintext recovery attacks.
findings.evidence: Negotiated cipher suite identifier: TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.

evidence_items.description: Negotiated cipher suite identifier: TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.

steps: Upgrade the affected mail server and client TLS libraries.
Remove the identified weak suites from that service using its version-specific cipher configuration; prefer supported AEAD suites.
Test client compatibility and verify the newly selected cipher in a fresh capture.

findings.recommendation: Disable obsolete cipher suites (RC4, 3DES, DES, EXPORT, NULL) on the mail server and require modern AEAD suites (e.g., AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305).

findings.title: Static Key Exchange Without Forward Secrecy
findings.plain_explanation: The session negotiated a static RSA key exchange cipher suite lacking Perfect Forward Secrecy. Compromise of the server private key allows retroactive decryption of past sessions.
findings.why_it_matters: Static key exchange allows an adversary who captures encrypted traffic to decrypt it retroactively if they acquire the server's private key in the future.
findings.evidence: Negotiated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA uses static RSA key exchange without ephemeral parameters.

evidence_items.description: Negotiated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA uses static RSA key exchange without ephemeral parameters.

steps: Prefer ephemeral ECDHE/DHE key exchange where supported; remove static RSA exchange after compatibility testing.
For TLS 1.3 inspect the selected key-share group; the cipher name alone does not prove forward secrecy.

findings.recommendation: Configure the mail server to disable static RSA key exchange suites and prioritize ECDHE key exchange.
